selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person will find in believing in Allah?
questions.answer: Great happiness, blessings, pleasure, and ease.

questions.question: What were the two men hoping to gain from their trip?
questions.answer: Enjoyment and business benefit.

questions.question: How did the first man view the land he entered?
questions.answer: He saw it as an evil and painful place.

questions.question: What does his seeing the whole country as a mourning place tell us?
questions.answer: He could not see any goodness or hope.

questions.question: What did he think he saw all around him besides enemies?
questions.answer: Dead bodies and crying, hopeless children.

questions.question: How did he understand the people around him?
questions.answer: As friends and close companions.

questions.question: How did the second man view other people?
questions.answer: He saw them as friends and like family.

questions.question: What did he tell the unhappy man about the source of his false vision?
questions.answer: It came from the darkness within his own self.

questions.question: What did the second man tell the first man was the real problem?
questions.answer: The ugliness inside him was making him see the outside world wrongly.

questions.question: What did he realize about the role of drink in his condition?
questions.answer: He realized it had driven him into madness.

questions.question: What is the main lesson the story is used to explain?
questions.answer: That belief in Allah brings joy, goodness, and ease.

questions.question: Which traveler had a bad view of life, and why?
questions.answer: The first traveler did, because he was arrogant, self-centered, and gloomy.

questions.question: What effect did his way of thinking have on the whole country in his eyes?
questions.answer: It made the whole place seem filled with grief.

questions.question: In his eyes, what were the people around him like?
questions.answer: They were enemies and strangers.

questions.question: What sounds of happiness did he hear?
questions.answer: Good wishes, thanks, and words praising Allah.

questions.question: What joyful things did he notice everywhere?
questions.answer: Festivals, remembering Allah, and happiness.

questions.question: What did the second man do when he met the first man again?
questions.answer: He understood his condition and gave him sincere advice.

questions.question: What was his response after his good experience?
questions.answer: He thanked Allah.

questions.question: What change took place in the unhappy man after the advice?
questions.answer: He recovered his senses and turned back in repentance.

questions.question: What would happen if he did that?
questions.answer: The false covering over his sight would be lifted and he would see the truth.

questions.question: Which verse is mentioned near the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The verse about those who believe in the Unseen.

questions.question: Why is the story called a comparison?
questions.answer: Because it shows two different kinds of people and how they see the same kind of journey very differently.

questions.question: What kinds of scenes made him upset wherever he went?
questions.answer: He thought he saw helpless people crying under harsh oppressors.

questions.question: What larger mood covered the whole country in his eyes?
questions.answer: Deep mourning and sadness.
